 Daily Stock Market Live
 Updated Mon, Nov 9 2026 4:26 PM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Dow surges 1,100 points, Nasdaq climbs more than 2% as tech rebounds from last week’s tumult: Live updates
 Sean Conlon Tanaya Macheel Lim Hui Jie Traders work on the floor of the American Stock Exchange (AMEX) at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York, US, on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Stocks surged on Monday, boosted by a decline in oil prices as well as gains in technology shares after last week's volatility.
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average popped 1,104.02 points, or 2.15%, to close at 52,389.75. The blue-chip index was supported by gains in stocks such as Goldman Sachs and Caterpillar . The S&P 500 rose 2.35% to end at 7,549.94 for its best day since April 8, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 2.74% to 25,253.14.
 With Monday's rally, the Dow is now above the level it closed on Election Day. The S&P 500 and tech-heavy Nasdaq still remain slightly below, however.
 Oil prices fell on Monday, lifting investor sentiment. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures dropped 4.38% to settle at $86.85 per barrel. International benchmark Brent slid 5.85% to $92.57 per barrel. 
 Friday's market partially rebounded from Thursday's brutal artificial intelligence-driven sell-off, as chip stocks recovered on renewed buying. However, concerns linger in the wake of the Democrats' strong midterm results, with investors fearing that tighter regulations on data center construction, energy use, and development costs could slow the AI infrastructure boom .
 The tech sector also focused on the bombshell announcement Sunday that Nvidia's board of directors is opening an investigation into co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a businesswoman who U.S. intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy. Nvidia shares closed down 4%.
 "Magnificent Seven" names were higher contrary to Nvidia. Amazon gained about 3%, while Tesla and Alphabet climbed 5.5% and 1%, respectively. Microsoft also added almost 3%.
 Other chip stocks advanced as well, with Broadcom popping nearly 9% and Advanced Micro Devices jumping 13%. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) — which dropped around 13% last week — rose more than 7%.
 The recent chip sell-off was "overdone," said Jay Hatfield, CEO at Infrastructure Capital Advisors. The turmoil was still "partially correct," he added, given that there "definitely is a policy overhang from the Democrats in both the short run, but, more importantly, in the long run from '28." To be sure, he believes data centers are ultimately "going to get built" in the U.S.
 For the broader market, Hatfield said that "it's not like the coast is clear" with Monday's bounce. In fact, he anticipates the S&P 500 will be rangebound through the end of the year.
 "There are still a lot of overhangs on the market," the CEO said, pointing to elevated oil prices as a result of the Middle East conflict as well as the Federal Reserve's interest rate outlook.
 This week , investors are looking ahead to key AI-related earnings — CoreWeave , Cisco and Applied Materials are all on deck — as they assess the outlook for tech and whether the recent sell-off has further to run. 
 They'll also watch for the releases of both the consumer price index on Tuesday and the producer price index on Friday, looking for clues on the Fed's next move.
 1 Hour Ago Stocks finish higher
 The three U.S. leading indexes popped on Monday.
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 1,104.02, or 2.15%, to settle at 52,389.75. The S&P 500 rose 2.35% to close at 7,549.94, while the Nasdaq Composite jumped 2.74% to 25,253.14.
 — Sean Conlon 
 2 Hours Ago Semiconductors ETF heads for best day since July
 Nurphoto | Nurphoto | Getty Images The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) surged more than 8% to start the week amid a revival in tech shares.
 Monday's advance in SOXX puts it on course for its best day since July 30.
 Monolithic Power , a maker of power modules, and semiconductor giant Advanced Micro Devices were among the biggest advancers in the ETF, up 16% and 14%, respectively.
 Nvidia was a standout underperformer, shedding more than 4%.
 — Darla Mercado and Gina Francolla 
 2 Hours Ago Energy is sole S&P 500 sector in the red
 S&P 500 energy was the only sector seeing losses in afternoon trading on Monday.
 The group was last down 0.3%, adding to its one-week loss of more than 8%.
 The remaining 10 S&P 500 sectors were in the green, led by industrials with a 4.2% gain. Consumer discretionary and information technology weren't too far behind, up 3.7% and 3%, respectively.
 — Sean Conlon 
 3 Hours Ago S&P 500 heads for its best day since April
 The S&P 500 was higher by more than 2% in afternoon trading Monday.
 The move put the broad market index on pace for its best day since April 8, when it gained 2.51%.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon S&P 500, 1-day — Nick Wells and Sean Conlon 
 4 Hours Ago GM’s move to the Nasdaq seen as positive by Citi
 General Motors' move to the Nasdaq on Nov. 17, and its possible inclusion in the Nasdaq-100 index as early as December, could bring increased investor visibility and focus to the overlooked automaker, according to Citi analyst Michael Ward.
 If GM joins the Nasdaq-100 index it "would have a 0.2% weighting in the Index which represents about $4.6 billion of buying, or 10% of the non-indexed market cap," he wrote.
 Additionally, he expects GM to buy back $10 billion in shares by the end of 2027, about 20% of the non-indexed market cap, which will support shares. If it joins, GM will become the cheapest stock in the index with the highest buyback yield, Ward noted. 
 CNBC recently said GM's switch to the Nasdaq could help it reframe its brand identity and boost its depressed valuation with the exposure to a new set of potential investors. Citi agreed. 
 "In our view, the structural improvements at GM and the North American industry have been missed, and if GM becomes part of the Nasdaq 100 Index, new investors will need to take a look which could bring added value to the stock," Ward wrote. The move helps reposition GM as a broad technology-first manufacturer, not just a combustion engine maker. "Consumer connection and complex manufacturing expertise position the auto sector to benefit from developing trends in energy storage, autonomous technologies, and connected platforms," wrote Ward. 
 Citi rates GM a buy with a $131 a share price target, which is more than 50% above Friday's close.
 — Justin Zacks 
 4 Hours Ago Stocks making big moves: First Solar, AST SpaceMobile, PDD Holdings
 An aerial view shows solar panels made by First Solar, during a tour of the Overland Park Solar Array in Toledo, Ohio, U.S., Oct. 5, 2021. Dane Rhys | Reuters First Solar : The provider of solar energy equipment slid more than 5% after Piper Sandler cut its price target on shares.
 AST SpaceMobile : Shares jumped 14% after the company announced a joint venture with Japanese company Rakuten on Monday.
 PDD Holdings : U.S.-listed shares shed 3.3% on the back of a downgrade at Morgan Stanley to equal weight from overweight.
 Check out the other names making moves in CNBC's live blog here .
 — Darla Mercado 
 5 Hours Ago Financial markets are 'likely to remain very news flow driven,' Wolfe Research says
 While stocks are bouncing back on Monday after last week's turbulence, they may not be over the hump yet.
 "With many investors unwilling to stick their neck out right before year-end, we struggle to find many positive catalysts for stocks over the near-term," said Chris Senyek, the firm's chief investment strategist, in a Monday note.
 Seeing downside risks, Senyek added, "We believe markets are likely to remain very news flow driven and need to hold critical technical support levels."
 Currently, the S&P 500 is trading just above its 200-day moving average.
 — Sean Conlon 
 6 Hours Ago Amid volatility, Oppenheimer says to focus on the fundamentals
 Traders work on the floor at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, New York, US, Nov. 6, 2026. Brendan McDermid | Reuters Stocks, primarily those exposed to the AI buildout, were hit last week following a bigger-than-expected victory by Democrats in the midterm elections. But Oppenheimer chief investment strategist John Stoltzfus thinks that the market can rebound, as it started on Monday.
 "So long as the underlying fundamentals that support economic growth and nurture revenue
 and profit growth have not dramatically deteriorated… the market can find opportunity to not just regain lost ground but even rise well above where it had been," Stoltzfus wrote in a Monday note. 
 This week, he said that all eyes will be on the inflation report set to be delivered Tuesday, particularly off a hot jobs report on Friday, as investors look to predict what the Federal Reserve will do with interest rates at its December meeting. And while some investors were nervous about the AI trade following Democratic victories last week, Stoltzfus doesn't share those concerns.
 "It would seem to us that it is much too early to predict the failure of AI to gain traction or achieve profitability," he said. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon S&P 500 5-day. — Davis Giangiulio 
 7 Hours Ago NYSE selects Avalanche as main blockchain for tokenized securities trading, settlement
 The New York Stock Exchange has chosen Avalanche as the primary blockchain network for processing clearing and settlement on its upcoming affiliated tokenized securities alternative trading system.
 The price of the Avalanche token ( AVAX ) jumped 8%, according to CoinGecko. Shares of Avalanche Treasury Corp , which was created to be the proxy trade for the blockchain network, jumped 12% in light trading.
 Avalanche is a six-year-old blockchain built for business. Unlike many networks aimed primarily at retail traders, Ava Labs, the company that helped develop Avalanche, has for years pursued financial institutions interested in tokenizing real-world assets and moving traditional financial infrastructure onto blockchain rails. Users include BlackRock, Franklin Templeton, Apollo, FIFA and the state of Wyoming.
 "At the NYSE, we're looking at how blockchain technology can expand what we offer in equities, and we're picking the right technology for each job," said Dennis Lee, head of digital issuance at NYSE, said in a statement. "The upcoming digital trading platform will support equities listed on a range of blockchains, though the ledger that records and settles trades needs to be fast and reliable, let us control who can take part, keep costs predictable, and have a large community of developers behind it."
 — Tanaya Macheel 
 8 Hours Ago Citi downgrades tech on positioning, sentiment concerns
 Citi is flagging the rotational turbulence beneath the index-level calm that equity markets have seen in recent days, bracing for more potential downside in the short term. The bank tactically downgraded "the US, Global Tech, and European Tech to Neutral (from Overweight)" in a Monday note. 
 "While fundamentals look attractive, positioning remains relatively neutral and could therefore adjust further into net short territory," Beata Manthey at Citi said. "We remain constructive on AI over the medium-term but would look for cleaner positioning and more stable AI sentiment (along with steady EPS revisions) before reestablishing our Overweight call."
 — Tobias Burns 
 8 Hours Ago Stocks open higher
 U.S. equities rose on Monday morning.
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 619 points, or 1.2%, shortly after 9:30 a.m. ET. The S&P 500 advanced 0.9%, while the Nasdaq Composite moved up 0.8%.
 — Sean Conlon 
 9 Hours Ago Oppenheimer upgrades AMD
 Lisa Su, chair and chief executive officer of Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD), during a fireside chat at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) in Bengaluru, India, on Thursday, Nov. 21, 2024. Gabriela Bhaskar | Bloomberg | Getty Images Advanced Micro Devices is on the verge of a big comeback after struggling of late, according to Oppenheimer. 
 The investment firm upgraded the chipmaker to outperform from perform. Its $600 price target implies 34% upside from Friday's close. 
 "We are raising estimates and upgrading shares of AMD on the heels of another bullish earnings call and recent fireside chat we hosted," analyst Rick Schafer said Sunday in a note to clients. "We see AMD emerging as a durable supplier of AI compute, with multi-gen customer wins and Helios rack-scale solutions supporting a materially larger [data center] business."
 "Annual Instinct product cadence and [AMD's open software stack] progress strengthen AMD's competitive positioning, while compute-heavy agentic AI drives incremental [graphics processing units] and … [central processing unit] demand," Schafer said.
 CNBC Pro subscribers can read more here .
 — Liz Napolitano 
 9 Hours Ago Nvidia, AMD and Eli Lilly among the stocks making big moves before the bell
 Nvidia : The artificial intelligence chip leader dropped nearly 5% after the company opened an investigation of CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a businesswoman, Alice Huang, who intelligence agencies allege is a Chinese spy.
 Advanced Micro Devices : Shares advanced 3.2% after Oppenheimer upgraded the chipmaker to outperform from market perform while assigning a price target of $600 per share. That suggest 34% upside to Friday's close.
 Eli Lilly : Shares increased nearly 2% after Canada's Drug Agency welcomed a positive recommendation to reimburse Lilly's treatment for early Alzheimer's called Kisunla for eligible adults on Friday.
 Check out the other names making moves in CNBC's live blog here .
 — Paulina Likos and Fred Imbert 
 10 Hours Ago Rubio calls Iranian demands 'outrageous and ridiculous'
 US Secretary of State Marco Rubio departs from Homestead Air Reserve Base in Homestead, Florida, on November 8, 2026. Brendan Smialowski | Afp | Getty Images U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has accused Iran of "outrageous and ridiculous" demands as efforts to reach a lasting resolution in the Middle East war appeared stalled.
 Speaking with reporters in Florida on Sunday evening before traveling to Paris for the G7 foreign ministers' meeting, Rubio indicated the two sides remain far apart on negotiations, after Tehran proposed shortening the timetable for restarting talks from seven days to two.
 Rubio said President Donald Trump would prefer to solve "this and every problem diplomatically," but added that "sometimes that's not possible, unfortunately." Read more .
 — Hugh Leask 
 11 Hours Ago Nasdaq defies Nvidia impact as Huang faces espionage affair probe
 Nasdaq defies Nvidia impact as Huang faces espionage affair probe 13 Hours Ago Nvidia stock falls 5% amid probe into CEO
 Nvidia shares were down around 5% in premarket trading Monday after the tech giant launched an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a businesswoman who intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy.
 The key question for investors will be whether Huang will remain as CEO, according to Dan Ives, senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co.
 "This is a black eye moment for Jensen and will spark multiple congressional inquiries at a minimum and will create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons," Ives said in a Sunday note.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon NVDA, 1-day Read the full story here .
 — April Roach 
 14 Hours Ago European stocks choppy in early trade
 European stocks got off to a mixed start on Monday, with the regional Stoxx 600 index opening lower before moving to a 0.4% gain by 8:20 a.m. in London.
 Mining stocks popped 1.7% as gold and copper prices bounced back from last week's downturn. 
 Italian bank Unicredit was the top performer, up 4.7% after its third-quarter net profit rose by a record 24% year-on-year and as it prepares to take control of Germany's Commerzbank .
 Luxury shares suffered, with LVMH , Moncler , Hermes , Kering , Burberry , Richemont and Christian Dior all trading slightly lower, as investors remained in risk-off mode and data showed mounting domestic inflation pressures in major market China. 
 Construction firm Hochtief  fell 5.3% after Spanish group ACS said it had not considered a tender offer for shares in the company, which is its German subsidiary. Bloomberg had reported ACS was considering buying the remaining Hochtief shares it does not own or a potential merger of the firms.
 — Jenni Reid 
 15 Hours Ago Nvidia's Frankfurt-traded shares drop 6% 
 Nvidia 's Frankfurt-traded shares were more than 6% lower in early European trading, as the company is rocked by an investigation into co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang 's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy .
 — Jenni Reid 
 15 Hours Ago Asia markets close higher, with Taiwan leading gains
 Asia-Pacific markets closed in broadly positive territory on Monday, amid a tech rebound and Taiwanese and Japanese stock gains.
 The Taiwan Weighted Index closed 4.94% up at 41,664.7, marking it largest one-day gain since 31 July. 
 The index was powered by gains in tech heavyweights Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Hon Hai Precision Industry — also known as Foxconn. 
 South Korea's Kospi fell 0.81% after a choppy session to end at 5,018.85, while the small-cap Kosdaq slipped 0.82% to 638.97.
 Japan's  Nikkei 225 closed 2.33% higher at 58,775.5, and the broad-based Topix saw a larger increase of 2.97% to 3,818.16.
 Mainland China's CSI 300 rose marginally to 4,056.11, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was flat in its last hour of trade.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 rose 0.1% to 9,029.7.
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 15 Hours Ago France's Crédit Agricole proposes Banco BPM merger
 View of the logo of a Credit Agricole bank agency at Lesneven in Brittany in France on September 08 2025. Vincent Feuray | Afp | Getty Images Crédit Agricole has proposed merging its Italian operation with Banco BPM in a deal that would create Italy's third-largest banking group.
 The French lender said in a statement Monday that the "friendly proposal" to engage its Italian peer in merger discussions is a "natural extension" of the long-term partnership between the pair.
 Under the deal, Crédit Agricole would increase its current 29.6% stake in Banco BPM to approximately 45% of the new combined entity.
 The proposal offers Banco BPM shareholders a 20% premium to the relative valuation of the businesses, based on estimated 2027 price-to-earnings multiples, and a 1 billion euro ($1.12 billion) special dividend, according to Crédit Agricole's announcement.
 The Paris-headquartered bank said the deal — which has been submitted to Banco BPM's board of directors for evaluation — could deliver 800 million in annual synergies, with about 24% 2027 earnings-per-share accretion expected.
 "This strategic project would create Italy's third-largest banking group, serving 6.5 million customers through more than 2,300 branches, by combining a strong local presence, financial strength, and business expertise," Crédit Agricole added.
 — Hugh Leask 
 16 Hours Ago European stocks heading for mixed open after volatile week 
 European bourses are heading for a weak open, according to IG futures data. France's CAC 40 , Germany's DAX and Italy's FTSE MIB were all seen slipping, though the U.K.'s FTSE 100 was last seen slightly higher. 
 It follows last week's post-midterms markets rollercoaster, with strong gains on Nov. 4 followed by a selloff on Nov. 5 and 6. The pan-European Stoxx 600 index ended the week 0.24% higher.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Stoxx 600 index. — Jenni Reid 
 16 Hours Ago UniCredit delivers “best quarter ever” as net profits surge 24%
 The logo of the Italian banking group UniCredit SpA is pictured on July 15, 2025 in Milan, Italy. Emanuele Cremaschi | Getty Images News | Getty Images UniCredit 's third-quarter net profit rose by a record 24% year-on-year to 3.3 billion euros ($3.68 billion), beating consensus estimates of 2.78 billion euros, as revenues reached 6.9 billion euros, up 12% year-on-year.
 The Italian bank, which is set to take control of German lender Commerzbank , also hiked its full-year profit guidance to full-year profit guidance to "well above" 11.5 billion euros, from more than 11 billion euros.
 Net interest income was up 5% over the quarter, and 8% year-on-year, while common equity tier (CET) 1 capital ratio — a measure of a bank's solvency — reached 15% during the period, up from 14.3% the previous quarter.
 "UniCredit has delivered its best quarter ever, and the best in the sector, beating across all KPIs: highest net profit growth, best RoTE and cost/income ratio and organic capital generation supporting best-in- class shareholder returns while increasing capital," CEO Andrea Orcel said in a statement.
 The Milan-headquartered lender said the Commerzbank acquisition would strengthen its pan-European footprint and boost earnings and shareholder distributions. It expects the remaining approvals to be greenlighted by European regulators later this month, with the deal's integration plan set to begin in the first quarter of 2027.
 — Hugh Leask 
 19 Hours Ago Bitcoin falls to lowest in more than two months with 200-day moving average in sight
 Nurphoto | Getty Images Bitcoin fell below $74,000 over the weekend to its lowest level since August before clawing back some of the losses.
 Ether, XRP, Hyperliquid and other cryptocurrencies also declined, according to pricing from Coingecko.
 "Bitcoin's renewed weakness is a concern," said Matt Maley of Miller Tabak + Co., who flagged the the test of September levels and said "a break below $75k would give it a key lower-low."
 However, he added that it would take a drop below the 200-day moving average around $73,000 "before it raised any serious warning flags."
 — Joanna Ossinger 
 20 Hours Ago China wholesale inflation hits highest in more than four years
 Producer prices in China grew at the fastest rate since June 2022, accelerating for the third month in a row.
 The PPI for October came in at 5.7%, compared to the 5.3% expected by economists polled by Reuters. The increase was driven by a sharp rise in prices in the mining and raw materials industries.
 Consumer inflation in China slowed to 0.7% in October, its first deceleration after two straight months of increases.
 Core inflation, which strips out food and energy prices, came in at 0.8%, down from the 1% seen in the month before.
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 22 Hours Ago Asian markets mostly down in opening trade; Japan gains
 Asia-Pacific markets mostly fell on Monday, with South Korean equities continuing their sharp sell-off from Friday.
 The benchmark Kospi index fell 0.69%, while the small-cap Kosdaq index declined 0.87%.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.31%, after initially starting the day in positive territory.
 The only outlier in the region was Japan, which saw the  Nikkei 225  gain 1.44% and the Topix climb 2.09%. 
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 23 Hours Ago Asia markets set for rebound after tech sell-off last week
 Asia-Pacific markets look stronger to start the week after last week's tech sell-off. 
 Futures for Japan's  Nikkei 225  in Chicago were at 58,520, while in Osaka they were last at 58,250 compared with the index's previous close of 57,434.77.
 Futures for Hong Kong's Hang Seng index last traded at 24,647, compared with the index's last close of 24,481.86.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was up 0.2% in early trading.
 Later Monday, investors will also look to inflation data out of China, with economists polled by Reuters expecting a reading of 0.8%, down slightly from September's 0.9%. 
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 23 Hours Ago Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with alleged Chinese spy
 Nvidia has opened an investigation into co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a businesswoman who intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy.
 Huang told Nvidia staff in an email on Sunday that he had an affair with the woman and that Nvidia's board of directors had opened an independent investigation into the spying allegations.
 An Nvidia spokesperson said that Huang was committed to continuing as CEO of Nvidia without interruption.
 Read Huang's email to Nvidia employees and the company board of directors' statement here .
 — Kif Leswing and Kamaron McNair 
 24 Hours Ago Stock futures open lower
 Stock futures fell to begin trading Sunday night.
 Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 93 points, or 0.2%. S&P 500 futures slid 0.4% and Nasdaq 100 futures tumbled 0.8%.
 — Tanaya Macheel
